title: Foundational-to-Research AI Engineering & Research Curriculum
executive_summary: Prerequisite-ordered, citation-verified learning path across 4 stages and 8 lessons generated for goal: "I want to become an AI engineer and eventually an AI researcher, starting from mathematical and programming foundations.". Grounded in 18 active knowledge chunks and 12 verified collected documents, with explicit reporting of 4 evidence and curation gaps.
rationale_for_ordering: The curriculum follows a strict topological sort over the concept prerequisite DAG: (1) Stage 1 establishes linear algebra, multivariable calculus, and reverse-mode backpropagation; (2) Stage 2 builds core generalization (Dropout regularization) and stochastic energy-based representation learning (Boltzmann machines & RBMs) atop gradient optimization; (3) Stage 3 scales depth via Deep Residual Learning (ResNet), resolves fixed-vector sequence bottlenecks via Bahdanau soft alignment, and synthesizes both into the recurrence-free Transformer architecture; (4) Stage 4 bridges engineering implementation to AI research methodology, ablation design, GFlowNets, and AI safety. Per platform governance, foundational prerequisites always precede recent architectures regardless of news recency in SRC-THE-BATCH.

lessons.title: Backpropagation, Reverse-Mode Automatic Differentiation, and Gradient Descent
learning_objectives: Formulate reverse-mode automatic differentiation over a computational graph using the chain rule.
Explain how backpropagation computes layer-wise error sensitivities efficiently in a single backward pass.

lessons.explanation: Backpropagation applies the multivariable chain rule recursively from the output loss backward through intermediate layers to compute exact gradients with respect to every weight. Rather than recomputing shared subexpressions, reverse-mode differentiation caches forward activations and propagates local sensitivities in O(W) time, enabling gradient descent optimization across multilayer networks. Retrieved primary evidence (Backpropagation, SRC-WIKIPEDIA): "Backpropagation In machine learning, backpropagation is a gradient computation method commonly used for training a neural network in computing parameter updates. lessons.title: Overfitting, Feature Co-Adaptation, and Dropout Regularization
learning_objectives: Diagnose overfitting and complex feature co-adaptation in overparameterized feedforward networks.
Implement inverted dropout during training and deterministic weight scaling at inference time.
Analyze dropout as approximate geometric model averaging across exponentially many thinned sub-networks.
lessons.explanation: When a large feedforward neural network is trained on a finite dataset, hidden units can co-adapt to fix errors made by other specific units, leading to brittle generalization on unseen test data. learning_objectives: Define the global energy function E(s) of a Boltzmann machine over symmetric binary stochastic units.

lessons.title: Deep Residual Learning (ResNet), Degradation vs. Overfitting, and Identity Shortcut Connections
learning_objectives: Distinguish the deep network training degradation problem from classical overfitting.
Reformulate stacked layers to learn residual mappings F(x) := H(x) - x with parameter-free identity shortcuts F(x) + x.
Analyze why identity skip connections preserve gradient flow across 100+ layer networks and Transformer blocks.
lessons.explanation: As neural networks grow deeper, training accuracy can saturate and degrade rapidly—not from overfitting, but because stacked nonlinear layers struggle to approximate identity mappings. By explicitly reformulating layers to learn residual functions F(x) = H(x) - x added to an identity shortcut x, Deep Residual Networks (ResNets) enable stable optimization at extreme depth without adding extra parameters or computational complexity. Retrieved primary evidence (Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition, SRC-ARXIV): "Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition Deeper neural networks are more difficult to train. We present a residual learning framework to ease the training of networks that are substantially deeper than those used previously. We expli..." lessons.title: Sequence-to-Sequence Bottlenecks and Joint Alignment & Translation (Bahdanau Attention)
learning_objectives: Identify why compressing variable-length input sequences into a single fixed-length vector bottlenecks encoder-decoder performance.
Formulate additive (Bahdanau) soft alignment scores e_{ij}, attention weights alpha_{ij}, and dynamic context vectors c_i.
Implement a Differentiable Attention Alignment module that searches over source annotations during decoding.
lessons.explanation: Classical encoder-decoder sequence models compress an entire input sentence into a single fixed-length vector, causing severe information loss on long sequences. Bahdanau, Cho, and Bengio (2014) resolved this bottleneck by allowing the decoder to softly search over all encoder hidden annotations at each generation step, computing differentiable alignment weights jointly with translation. Retrieved primary evidence (Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate, SRC-ARXIV): "encodes a source sentence into a fixed-length vector from which a decoder generates a translation. In this paper, we conjecture that the use of a fixed-length vector is a bottleneck in improving the performance of this basic encoder-deco..." [chk_cbf933bd5853089c] [chk_fb78852dfe1044b4] [chk_f38d9214a536ff59].

lessons.explanation: Vaswani et al. (2017) introduced the Transformer, a sequence transduction architecture based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. lessons.explanation: Transitioning from an AI engineer who implements architectures to an AI researcher who advances the field requires rigorous hypothesis formulation, controlled ablations, and awareness of long-horizon safety and governance challenges. In our curated repository, verified research portals from Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio define key themes in representation learning, Generative Flow Networks, and AI safety, while also highlighting where full-text primary papers remain to be collected. Retrieved primary evidence (Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition, SRC-ARXIV): "Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition Deeper neural networks are more difficult to train.
